history.dynasty: ISKCON (International Society for Krishna Consciousness); built 2005
history.summary: ISKCON Temple Rajahmundry is a modern Krishna temple built by ISKCON in 2005 and inaugurated on 9 August 2006, per holidify. It has four altars for the deities of the four compass directions, surrounded by the ten incarnations of the Lord. The temple draws 1,000-1,500 devotees daily, 6,000-8,000 on Sundays, and runs a Govinda Srinivasa Abhishekam at 6:30 PM every Friday; it celebrated its 10th anniversary in 2016 (per The Hindu).

name: ISKCON Rajahmundry
town_description: Rajahmundry (officially Rajamahendravaram) is a historic city on the eastern bank of the Godavari River in coastal Andhra Pradesh, often called the cultural capital of the state. Founded around the 11th century by the Eastern Chalukyas (Raja Raja Narendra), it was the first capital of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty and later the birthplace of the Telugu language's classical literature. Today it is a major rail and road hub with its own airport, and its river ghats (Gowthami, Pushkar) are among the busiest pilgrimage spots on the Godavari.

travel.airport: Rajahmundry Airport (approx. 15-18 km; limited domestic flights) (verify); Vijayawada Airport (approx. 160 km) for wider connectivity.
travel.railway: Rajahmundry Junction (approx. 5 km per traveltriangle), a major station on the Howrah-Chennai main line.
travel.road: The temple stands at Hare Krishna Land, beside Godavari Bund Road, Gowthami Ghat, T Nagar; autos, cabs and city buses from Rajahmundry Junction take 10-20 minutes (traveltriangle cites ~5 km/5 minutes by cab - verify locally).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for the pleasantest weather; Janmashtami (August-September) is the grandest festival but the most crowded - 50,000+ visitors per holidify.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:30 AM to 1:00 PM and 4:30 PM to 8:30 PM daily, per holidify and traveltriangle (verify - hours may shift on festival days). No entry fee; Govinda Srinivasa Abhishekam at 6:30 PM every Friday.
